solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: British caprice ordered manifestation of armed power

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whimsical British impulse is described as a show of military force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'armed power' reads as military might, but it is literal: the power in an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper arm is what bulges when an arm shows its strength, so it is a cryptic picture of arm power.

clue.text: Surgery, evidently reversible, seen in China

parts.note: an operation is an OP, a common abbreviation

indicators.note: the surgery abbreviation is followed by itself turned backwards, as if it were plainly reversible

explanation.surface: A surgical procedure that can apparently be undone is observed in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate. The capital C hides that it is not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a china is a mate, and an oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague.

clue.text: Set piece player involved in scrum

definitions.meaning: an item of stage property, a piece of the set in a theatre
a rugby forward who packs down at the front of the scrum

explanation.surface: A rugby player features in a set-piece move such as a scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set piece' is a rugby term for scrums and lineouts, which makes the two halves look like one rugby phrase; it is really theatre scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre stage properties are props, and the two forwards either side of the hooker in rugby are props.

clue.text: Live fish on board as well?

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting inside the steamship letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the vessel one is on board
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether live fish are also carried aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' places IDE within SS (steamship), a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides and as well are synonyms meaning in addition, also.

clue.text: Mugs people in street for amount to be paid

parts.note: mugs are gullible fools, asses

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: men stands for people in general

explanation.surface: Muggers on the street demand a sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mugs' looks like a verb (to rob) but is a plural noun meaning fools.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a sum levied or charged, such as a tax bill or a valuation demanding payment.

clue.text: Hairy pet for each Welshwoman on boat

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
Sian is a Welsh woman's name
a cat is a catamaran or a cat-rigged sailing boat

explanation.surface: A furry animal is shared out, one per Welsh woman on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is famous for its long, luxuriant coat, making it the hairiest of domestic felines.

clue.text: Grammatical device that one encounters in Hansard?

definitions.text: Grammatical device that one encounters in Hansard?

parts.words: Grammatical device that one encounters in Hansard?
parts.note: Hansard is the written record of what is said in the UK Parliament, so it literally holds speeches that have been reported, as well as the indirect style grammarians name

explanation.surface: A question about which grammatical construction appears in the parliamentary record.
explanation.walkthrough: Hansard is the official printed transcript of debates in the British Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect speech, the grammar term for relaying what someone said, also literally describes parliamentary speeches written up in a record.

clue.text: Toxic gas swirling in mix once on B-road?

indicators.note: swirling suggests the letters of the following words being whirled around into a new order

explanation.surface: Poisonous fumes swirl around in the traffic mix on a minor road.
explanation.walkthrough: A B-road is a minor British road; the hyphen is ignored in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourless, odourless gas from exhausts is poisonous because it binds to haemoglobin.

clue.text: Calm cop discomposed by cool criminal partner

indicators.note: discomposed means flustered, but here literally de-composed, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: to cool something is to ice it

explanation.surface: An unruffled policeman is thrown by a criminal's composed partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discomposed' makes ACCOMPL from CALM COP.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is someone who helps another commit a crime, a partner in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Bird lost taking off close to ditch

indicators.note: the final letter of the castle ditch is removed, close meaning end

parts.note: a moat is a defensive ditch around a castle

explanation.surface: A bird disappears as it takes flight near a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off close to' removes the T at the end of MOAT. 'taking off' suggests flight, but it means removing.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a giant flightless New Zealand bird hunted to extinction, so it is lost to the world.

clue.text: Bruised and cut on the tongue

indicators.note: on the tongue means as spoken, so the word for cut is pronounced

parts.note: to saw is to cut, and saw is also the past tense of see

explanation.surface: Someone has a bruised and cut tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SAW and SORE are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruised spot is tender and painful to touch, which is what being sore means.

clue.text: Runner outside failing to finish

indicators.note: failing to finish means the word for outside loses its final letter

parts.note: the skin is the outside of a body or fruit

explanation.surface: A runner on the outside lane does not complete the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is a runner in the sense of a sledge or blade that glides.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner on which one glides over snow, like the runners of a sledge.

clue.text: Ms Principal seeing agent's coming round

indicators.note: the agent's letters come around the principal, enclosing it

parts.note: an agent is a spy, plus the possessive S
a master is a principal or head, as of a college

explanation.surface: A Ms Principal, a headteacher, sees an agent who is visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ms' is not the title but the plural of M, the head of British intelligence in the Bond stories.
explanation.definitionFit: M, the fictional head of MI6, runs secret agents, so several such Ms are intelligence chiefs.

clue.text: Be satirical about Dutch house plant

parts.note: to mock is to ridicule or satirise
the House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty

explanation.surface: A satirist pokes fun at a Dutch house plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house plant' reads as one phrase, but 'house' belongs to the royal House and 'plant' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Philadelphus, a garden shrub with fragrant white blossom resembling citrus flowers, has this common name.

clue.text: Called out random number to be put in order

indicators.note: called out means said aloud, as a bingo caller announces numbers

parts.note: random means stray, as in a stray bullet, and the number is ten

explanation.surface: A bingo-style caller announces a random number to be put in order.
explanation.walkthrough: STRAY TEN said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten things is to tidy them or set them right, putting them in order.

clue.text: Man one to be flayed soon

indicators.note: to flay is to strip the skin, so the outer letters of the two words are peeled off, leaving what lies hidden inside

explanation.surface: A man is to be flogged before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be flayed' strips M and E, the outer letters of MANONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or presently, as in 'I'll see you anon'.

clue.text: Enigmatic alumnus tested outside clubs

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the word for tested goes outside the clubs abbreviation

parts.note: something tested and proven is sure, reliable
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A puzzling former student was tested in the open air of the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is unclear or hard to understand, much as something enigmatic is mysterious.

clue.text: What's kept in hillsides and vales is delightful!

definitions.text: What's kept in hillsides and vales
definitions.meaning: a reference to the Welsh song We'll Keep a ... in the Hillsides, whose words also keep one in the vales
as an adjective, gladly received and pleasing, as in a most agreeable change

explanation.surface: Something treasured in the Welsh countryside is a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'We'll Keep a Welcome' is a much-loved Welsh anthem of hospitality.
explanation.definitionFit: The song promises hospitality waiting in the Welsh hills, and the word as adjective means gladly received and pleasing.

clue.text: Chapel area in gold and blue

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
blue is the colour of the Conservative Party, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: A chapel area is decorated in gold and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel or place for private prayer.

clue.text: Shakespearean prince with love that could make one light-headed?

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince is in love and giddy with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light-headed' usually means dizzy, but here it is literal: having light around the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of light shown around a saint's head would literally make that head lit up.

clue.text: Irish woman can start to gossip — that's tiresome

parts.note: Rita is a woman's name
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word gossip

explanation.surface: An Irish woman can start gossiping, which is tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating is annoying and wearing, as is something tiresome.

clue.text: Notice nothing that causes trouble

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Ignore the idle remark, since it only causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Large American lorry stuck in Brighton

indicators.note: stuck in means the letters are lodged inside the town's name

explanation.surface: A big American truck is stuck in the seaside town of Brighton.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a resort town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage a rig is an articulated truck, a tractor-trailer.

clue.text: Hawk-headed god entertains explosive Titaness

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the god's name holds the explosive

parts.note: Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown with a falcon's head
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A bird-headed Egyptian deity plays host to an explosive Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Rhea was one of the Titans, mother of Zeus and wife of Cronus.

clue.text: Dissent from champion hugging the heartless mistress

indicators.note: hugging means the champion wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a champion is a hero, someone who fights for a cause

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter

parts.note: a doxy is an old word for a mistress or lover

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a champion embracing a cold-hearted mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' is the deletion signal on 'the', and 'hugging' sets that shortened word inside the champion. A doxy is an archaic term for a mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterodoxy is departure from accepted belief, so it amounts to dissent from orthodoxy.

clue.text: Bay tree not wide

indicators.note: not means the following item is to be left out

parts.note: the rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A bay tree is described as narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay tree' looks like the laurel; 'Bay' is a horse and 'tree' starts the wordplay. A wide in cricket is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are horse coat colours, and a bay roan is a reddish horse with white hairs mixed in.

clue.text: Tax on goods and service

definitions.meaning: a levy charged on imports, as in customs and excise
a task or obligation performed, as in being on active service

explanation.definitionFit: Customs charges on imports are levies of this name, and service owed or done is also called this.

clue.text: Such suits as may look well on Amazon?

definitions.text: Such suits as may look well on Amazon?

parts.words: Such suits as may look well on Amazon?
parts.note: legend says the Amazon warriors removed one breast to draw a bow more easily, so a jacket cut for one side would suit them

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders which suits would look good bought on the online store.
explanation.walkthrough: Amazon is not the retailer but a woman of the mythical warrior race, said to have cut off one breast.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket with one row of buttons and a narrow overlap is described this way, which fits the one-breasted Amazon of legend.
